exemplars.title: Beyond Text Generation: Supporting Writers with Continuous Automatic Text Summaries
exemplars.why: Continuously recomputed paragraph summaries appear as margin annotations beside the text being authored, making the source, automatic derivation, adjacency, and non-committal commentary role explicit.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It is more canonical than GPTFootprint because the adjacent output is unmistakably generated commentary on the artifact, rather than a display of calculated usage metrics.

exemplars.title: GPTFootprint: Increasing Consumer Awareness of the Environmental Impacts of LLMs
exemplars.why: Its always-visible side panel updates environmental-impact information during the primary activity, clearly establishing persistence, automatic refresh, spatial adjacency, and a read-only derived display.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It outranks Marco because the evidence explicitly establishes an always-visible side panel, while Marco’s quote does not confirm that its two views are spatially co-present.

exemplars.title: Marco: Supporting Business Document Workflows via Collection-Centric Information Foraging with Large Language Models
exemplars.why: Interaction in the Notebook View automatically drives derived, collection-level aggregation in a distinct Table View, providing a clear invocation-free and asymmetric dependency between working and commentary regions.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It narrowly beats DiagLink because its panel content is explicitly derived through automatic aggregation, whereas DiagLink may merely expose collected fields rather than generated commentary.

notes: The final selection retains the consensus top three, but Marco’s score is reduced slightly because the quoted evidence does not explicitly establish persistent spatial adjacency or read-only status. The strongest two picks have direct evidence for placement and live updating; however, GPTFootprint’s output is calculated telemetry rather than generative prose, so readers should treat it as a structural exemplar rather than a prototypical content-generation case. Marco is the least secure pick: its automatic cross-view derivation is clear, but co-presence is inferred from the named views rather than demonstrated by the quote. Plotania was not promoted despite its novelty because its evidence does not establish the authored source, automatic edit-to-refresh dependency, or side-panel placement; DiagLink was not promoted because its right-hand display may be a structured record of collected information rather than running generated commentary.
